title: Compat entry
description: @minerva/lib-core/compat: @novel-isr/ui's exact export names and prop shapes, implemented with Minerva.

entries.title: Entries
entries.text: Three JavaScript entries mirror @novel-isr/ui's: compat (client, "use client"), compat/theme-utils (server-safe, no banner) and compat/monaco (optional Monaco peers). Load compat.css after style.css for the --ui-* tokens.

guarantees.title: What compat guarantees
guarantees.names: Every runtime export (135) and every type (163) of @novel-isr/ui, with the same names and prop shapes.
guarantees.strings: novel's original built-in strings (mostly Chinese) are passed as explicit props, so the output does not depend on lib-core's language.
guarantees.hooks: The same ui-* class names, data-* attributes and component custom properties, so app stylesheets keep working.
guarantees.tokens: compat.css aliases every --ui-* token to a Minerva token (exact novel values per palette where Minerva has no token) and ships novel's reset and motion utilities.
guarantees.sideEffects: The entry has no side effects: importing it never changes lib-core's locale or theme.
guarantees.proof: Proved by tests: an export coverage test, compat tests with props from novel's own tests and the apps, and novel's e2e suites run against compat.
guarantees.note: Compat is a migration aid: new code should use the native Minerva API.
